All geometry uses nm, ps, atomic mass units, elementary charge, degrees unless radians are explicitly selected, and periodic minimum-image distances when PBC is enabled. Reconstruct molecules made whole before center-of-mass, fitting, or molecular-dipole calculations when requested. A center of mass is `sum(m_i r_i)/sum(m_i)`; a center of geometry uses equal weights. RMSD is the square root of the mean squared displacement after any selected least-squares rotational/translational fit. Radius of gyration is `sqrt(sum(w_i |r_i-r_c|^2)/sum(w_i))`. Inertia tensors are mass-weighted, symmetric, diagonalized, and their eigenvectors orthonormal; axes and eigenvalues have deterministic ordering/sign conventions.

Histogram bins are half-open except the last, use the requested width/range, and normalization integrates to the appropriate count or probability. Correlation at lag `t` averages all origins that possess that lag and is normalized at lag zero only when requested. Derivatives, integrations, FFTs and covariance eigenproblems must be calculated from input values, not fabricated. Selections distinguish atom positions, residue centers, and molecule centers. Time, axis, bin count, normalization, PBC, fitting, weighting and group choices must materially affect results. Empty bins must yield defined zero values rather than NaN/Inf unless a command explicitly reports an undefined conversion.

item.text: The specification defines a large multicall interface, with especially precise contracts for help, parser diagnostics, and several text-file workflows. I’m building reusable fixture helpers and keeping tests isolated so a single failure won’t prevent the rest of the suite from running.

## Spec 13

`pdb2gmx -f PDB -o STRUCT -p TOP` builds a chemically consistent all-atom topology and processed coordinates using force-field data found through `GMXLIB`. `-ff` accepts installed AMBER (including amber03 and variants), CHARMM27, GROMOS43a1/variants, and OPLS-AA identifiers; `-water` accepts compatible `tip3p`, `tip4p`, `spc`, and `spce`. Invalid force fields fail and list available choices. For `-ff nonexistent`, the diagnostic contains the exact sentence opening `Could not find force field 'nonexistent' in current directory, install tree or`; the following line completes it with `GMXLIB path.`. Recognize standard amino-acid residues, chains, termini and disulfide-capable cysteines; unknown residues fail clearly unless an explicit missing-atom policy permits processing.

Add hydrogens and termini atoms by templates; `-ignh` discards input hydrogen positions and rebuilds, `-heavyh` increases hydrogen masses by transferring mass, and `-deuterate` produces deuterated masses/naming behavior. Detect disulfide bonds geometrically using `-dist` and `-angle`; `-ss` controls interactive choices. `-chainsep` controls chain/TER separation. `-renum` renumbers residues, `-nocmap` omits CMAP interactions, `-missing` allows missing atoms, and `-v` gives detailed processing output. Generate valid bonds/angles/dihedrals/exclusions, molecule declarations, force-field includes, water model, and optional position restraints `-i` with `-posrefc`; topology atom counts/names must match coordinates. On standard output report the resulting system charge in the form `Total charge VALUE e`; processing the supplied dipeptide with `-ff amber03 -water tip3p` prints exactly `Total charge -0.000 e`.

Chain and special-bond discovery are also observable parts of the interface. With `-chainsep ter`, the supplied PDB containing two TER-separated chains prints a standard-output summary beginning exactly `There are 2 chains`. While checking geometrically possible disulfides, standard error contains the exact heading `Special Atom Distance matrix:` and identifies cysteine entries with the literal residue token `CYS`; for a detected pair it then reports a line of the form `Linking CYS-25 SG-14 and CYS-80 SG-477...`.
